one_liner: Header-only, exact, multithreaded mesh Booleans for open, closed and non-manifold meshes; beats CGAL corefinement.
what_it_does: Computes regularized Boolean set operations on 3D regions bounded, fully or partly, by triangle meshes. It handles open, closed and non-manifold boundaries, nested or hollow regions, and the empty and full regions. The API is templated on a CGAL kernel: wrap each triangle soup in kigumi::Region<K, FaceData>, build a Boolean_region_builder{a, b} once, then call it with any of the 16 Boolean_operator values. Per-face user data is carried through to the output. It is not a drop-in for CGAL's corefine_and_compute_* functions, which take CGAL Surface_mesh objects.
how_it_is_fast: It implements an optimized version of Barki, Guennebaud and Foufou (2015), 'Exact, robust, and efficient regularized Booleans on general 3D meshes'. An AABB tree finds candidate face pairs. Intersections are found symbolically (which triangle features cross) before any exact point is built, intersected faces are re-triangulated with a CGAL constrained Delaunay triangulation, and faces are classified locally and then by propagating tags across connected components, so only one exact point-in-soup test is needed per component. Every stage (pair finding, symbolic intersection, exact-point evaluation, triangulation, global classification) runs on std::threads that pull work items from a shared atomic index; the README shows 4.6 s sequential vs 1.1 s parallel on the closed case.
when_to_use: You need exact (EPECK) Booleans and CGAL's corefinement is too slow: closed case 27.2 s (CGAL) vs 4.6 s sequential and 1.1 s parallel in the author's run.
Inputs are open surfaces (terrain, water surface) or non-manifold meshes, where CGAL corefinement, libigl, Manifold and MCUT all FAILED in the README table and kigumi finished in 0.1-2.4 s.
You want many Boolean results from the same pair: the builder does the expensive mixing once and each operator call only extracts faces.
Per-face attributes (material IDs, labels) must survive the operation.
Multi-core desktops or servers: the code scales by thread count (KIGUMI_NUM_THREADS or a Threading_context).
when_not_to_use: Closed, manifold meshes where approximate results are acceptable: Manifold was faster (1.3 s sequential, 0.2 s parallel vs 4.6 s and 1.1 s) in the same table.
Inputs with degenerate faces or self-intersections: the README says the result is undefined and may crash or produce broken meshes; Corefine throws 'mesh has self-intersections'.

Proprietary binaries without a CGAL commercial licence: it needs CGAL's 2D Triangulations package (GPL or commercial) as well as the LGPL kernel, so the MIT label does not make the whole stack permissive.
Projects that cannot take C++20 plus Boost, CGAL and fast_float as dependencies.

You need a mature, widely deployed engine: 54 stars, version 0.1.0 in vcpkg.json, one maintainer; issue #33 reports a wrong union fixed by nudging the meshes, and issue #28 reports a 273 s run with no visible resolution.

integration.dependencies: CGAL (2D and 3D Linear Geometry Kernel, 2D Triangulations), Boost (container, container_hash, endian, iterator, range, unordered), fast_float; the repo pins all of them through a vcpkg submodule
integration.min_toolchain: C++20 (CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20, designated initializers); CMake 3.18+; build docs exist for Windows, macOS (Xcode 16 plus Homebrew LLVM) and Ubuntu
integration.platforms: any platform CGAL and Boost support; documented builds for Windows, macOS and Ubuntu
integration.thread_safety: Internally multithreaded with std::thread. The thread count lives in a thread_local Threading_context (default hardware_concurrency); concurrent calls from user threads are not documented.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — uses CGAL kernels and exact arithmetic like PMP corefinement, but takes kigumi Region/Triangle_soup inputs rather than CGAL Surface_mesh, and the operator set and region semantics differ.

gotchas: Corefine.h prints progress lines ('Finding face pairs...', 'Triangulating...') to std::cout unconditionally, so a library user gets stdout noise.
Open meshes must be clipped by a common convex region; otherwise you get the FIRST/SECOND_MESH_PARTIALLY_INTERSECTS warning and results can be wrong (see issue #33). Check builder.warnings().
Inconsistently oriented inputs make the builder throw std::runtime_error, and faces with more than three vertices are read as triangle fans.
The README table predates the 2026-07-20 Autorefinement change, and it gives no mesh sizes or CGAL version; the input meshes are generated by tools/gen_bench_meshes.sh.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick kigumi over Manifold, MeshLib or trueform when you need exact results or have open or non-manifold inputs. Manifold is several times faster on closed manifold meshes but approximate and fails on the other cases. Hob3l is narrower: it targets OpenSCAD CSG export.
verified_claims_summary: Intersection of two generated mesh pairs on a 16-core MacBook Pro 14-inch M4 (2024, M4 Max-class), built with Homebrew Clang 22.1.1 in CMake Release, excluding I/O. kigumi took 4.6 s single-threaded and 1.1 s parallel on the closed case vs 27.2 s for CGAL PMP corefinement with EPECK and 39.3 s for libigl's CGAL-exact mesh_boolean. On the open case it took 2.4 s vs 3.2 s. These are first-party numbers from a single machine.
status_note: Maintained by one author (MIT, 54 stars, last commit 2026-08-31, Autorefinement added 2026-07-20). It is copyable, but any shipped binary carries CGAL's GPL obligations unless CGAL is licensed commercially.
